dedupe_keys.name: bundesnetzagentur emf database of radio transmitter sites emf datenbank

description: The EMF-Datenbank of Germany's Federal Network Agency is an online map of every fixed radio transmitter site that needs a site certificate (Standortbescheinigung) under the German rules on electromagnetic field exposure, together with the places where the agency has carried out EMF measurement campaigns. It covers mobile base stations, broadcasting transmitters and other radio installations; reported figures give about 187,000 radio base stations at about 85,000 antenna sites. For each site the database shows the address, the responsible regional office and data from the site certificate, such as the type of radio system, mounting height, main beam direction and safety distances, and the certificates can be downloaded as PDF files. Since October 2024 it also shows which mobile network operators use each site, although not which antennas belong to which operator, and it does not state the mobile generation or frequencies. Coverage: all of Germany, continuously updated. Format and access: free online map and search, with PDF certificates; no bulk download or open licence was found. Caveats: site positions may be off by up to 80 metres; low-power installations below 10 W are not included. Simulation uses: locating mobile and broadcast sites for hazard exposure and coverage models, operator site sharing for interdependency analysis and a German counterpart to national antenna registers. Related records: the French ANFR and Spanish Infoantenas registers and Ofcom Sitefinder cover other countries, and the German Breitbandatlas covers coverage.
